captured_from: A real Stop payload from Claude Code 2.1.280, captured 2026-09-29 by a raw dump hook in a scratch project under d:\pantesting at the end of a headless `claude -p --permission-mode default` turn. The keys, their order and their value types are the captured ones. The values are synthetic: the ids, the paths and the final message are replaced. `permission_mode` keeps the captured value, and background_tasks is the empty list the turn-final Stop carried. The previous version of this fixture (2026-09-17) was derived from the fields hooks/pan-stop-guard.js reads, `stop_hook_active` and `cwd`, and lacked six keys the host sends: scratchpad_dir, prompt_id, permission_mode, last_assistant_message, background_tasks and session_crons.

placeholders.{{TRANSCRIPT_PATH}}: absolute path of the session transcript
placeholders.{{PROJECT_DIR}}: absolute path of the project whose .planning/ tree arms or disarms the guard
placeholders.{{SCRATCHPAD_DIR}}: the host's per-session scratchpad directory; no PAN hook reads it

notes: `stop_hook_active: false` is the arming case — the first stop attempt of a chain. The e2e test flips it to true on the same fixture to prove the one-shot rule, so the fixture deliberately carries the value that lets the guard fire. The loop-safety semantics ("the host sets stop_hook_active on stop attempts that follow a stop-hook block") are documented in docs/HOOKS.md and pinned in both spellings by tests/stop-guard-hook.test.cjs. The same capture showed a Stop that fired while a subagent was still running: background_tasks then listed that agent ({id, type: subagent, status: running, description, agent_type}). The guard does not read the field.
